The most likely cause in that text is the call `_actions(state, types, links)` while the definition is `_actions(state, types)` (two positional parameters) — an arity mismatch. That is a hypothesis about the recorded TypeError, not a verified diagnosis.

Repair applied (minimal, keeps the same public contract, the exact domain semantics, and the deterministic BFS strategy):
- Thread the parsed `links` relation explicitly into action generation instead of the id()-keyed `_LINK_CACHE` module-level dict, which was both dead code (`_compute_links` always returned {}) and a cross-call contamination hazard.
- Make `_actions` take (state, ctx) and keep the three grounded operators with the domain's exact argument order: walk(start, end, man), pickup_spanner(l, s, m), tighten_nut(l, s, m, n).
- Restore strict precondition checks per the supplied domain: walk requires at(m,start) and link(start,end); pickup_spanner requires at(m,l) and at(s,l); tighten_nut requires at(m,l), at(n,l), carrying(m,s), useable(s), loose(n), with effects not loose(n), not useable(s), tightened(n).
- Move all type filtering into the per-call `ctx` sets so no planning run depends on objects that are absent from this instance's declared types.
- Determinism: every derived collection is sorted; no reliance on set iteration order; inputs are only read (all inputs normalized into new sets/tuples).
- Bounds preserved: at most 1000 actions and an expansion cap returning the empty plan rather than an unbounded search.

Not claimed: that this fixes every hidden instance, that the plan is optimal or physically realizable beyond the stated domain, or that the check generalizes beyond the ten recorded learning-scope tasks.
